name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
description: Monthly food assistance loaded onto an electronic EBT card, usable at most grocery stores and farmers markets across New York City.
income_threshold: Varies by household size and income (up to 130%-200% FPL); some non-citizens may qualify.

name: Cash Assistance (Family Assistance & Safety Net)
description: Monthly cash support for families and individuals in need, often paid via debit card or directly to landlords for rent relief.
income_threshold: Based on gross income, resources, and household family size.

name: Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE)
description: Freezes rent for tenants with a qualifying disability benefit (SSI, SSDI, VA disability); landlord receives a property tax credit for the difference.
income_threshold: Household income $50,000/yr or less; rent must exceed one-third of monthly income.

name: Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE)
description: Freezes the rent for head-of-household tenants age 62+ living in rent-regulated apartments, preventing landlord rent increases.
income_threshold: Household income $50,000/yr or less; rent must exceed one-third of monthly income.
required_documents: Proof of rent / current & previous lease

name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher
description: Voucher that covers part of rent for lower-income families renting from private landlords; tenant pays roughly 30-40% of income toward rent.

name: Head Start / Early Head Start
organization: U.S. Dept. of Health & Human Services
description: Free early childhood education, meals, and health screenings for low-income families with children age 5 and under.
income_threshold: At or below federal poverty guidelines (e.g. ~$33,000/yr for household of 4).
required_documents: Proof of income or public benefits receipt (SNAP/SSI)

name: Pre-K for All
description: Free full-day, play-based Pre-K program for four-year-olds at public schools, DOE-run centers, and community partner organizations.
income_threshold: No income requirement; universal for all 4-year-old NYC residents.

name: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)
description: Federal, state, and city tax credit for working individuals and families with low to moderate income; averages about $2,300 combined.
income_threshold: Single without children: up to ~$19,104/yr; married with children: up to ~$68,675/yr.
required_documents: Social Security numbers for filer and all dependents

name: Child Tax Credit (CTC)
description: Federal and NY State tax credit for families raising children, worth up to ~$3,200 per child under 4 and ~$2,700 for ages 4-16.
required_documents: Social Security numbers for filer and qualifying child dependents

name: Qualified Health Plans (QHP)
description: Subsidized private health insurance marketplace plans covering preventive care and pre-existing conditions at low or zero cost.
income_threshold: Subsidy amount depends on household income; lower incomes may qualify for Medicaid or Essential Plan.

name: School Tax Relief Program (STAR)
organization: NYS Dept. of Taxation / NYC DOF
description: Annual credit that lowers property taxes for eligible homeowners; Enhanced STAR gives a larger benefit to seniors 65+.
income_threshold: Basic STAR: household income $500,000/yr or less; Enhanced STAR: ~$110,750/yr or less.
required_documents: Social Security numbers of all owners
Prior federal or state tax return
Proof of primary homeownership and residency

name: Comprehensive After School System (COMPASS NYC)
organization: NYC Dept. of Youth & Community Development
description: Free afterschool programs for K-12 students offering homework help, STEM, arts, and sports, typically 3 hours/day.
income_threshold: No income requirement; open to all NYC students K-12.
required_documents: Proof of child's identity (birth certificate or school record)
